newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher on mix of bullish inputs.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher on mix of bullish inputs.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher on fund buying, commercial short covering and spillover strength from a rally in CBOT soybeans, traders said.

CBOT soybeans surged at the opening and ended broadly higher on fears that a strike called for Wednesday by port workers at a key Brazilian port could spread to other ports across the country, thereby paralyzing exports.
"We saw fund buying by (E. D. & F. Man International), commercial short covering by Continental and Dreyfus -- and both of those worked in tandem with the beans," a trader said.
KCBT wheat settled 3-1/4 to eight cents per bushel higher, with nearby March up 6-1/4 cents at $4.29-1/4. May was up 6-1/2 cents at $4.06-1/2.
Gains in new crop July were limited by ideas the HRW wheat crop is in extremely good shape. Monthly condition reports from HRW growing states were due out later Monday

Cargill Investor Services was a key player, selling 5.5 million July bushels. Commission house Rosenthal Collins bought 2.7 million May and Man bought 1.0 million May and 2.5 million July, traders said. Commercial firm Dreyfus was said to have been a late buyer of KCBT July against CBOT July.
